searched: Read the federal monthly generator file for September 2026 for every Wisconsin gas and oil generator and matched each plant to GEM, which turned up Fitchburg and Elk Mound as operating plants GEM lacks and the missing 2004 block at Riverside.
Read the MISO queue file in full and answered all 44 Wisconsin requests that need an answer, adding four gas requests that no GEM plant covers.

Read the state draft Strategic Energy Assessment of June 2026 in full, including Table 2-2 on fuel switches and Table B-8 on planned gas additions, and tied every row to a GEM plant or a batch record.

Read WEC Energy Group's September and November 2026 investor presentations, Alliant's 2025 annual report and third quarter 2026 report, Madison Gas and Electric's 2025 annual report, Dairyland's 2025 annual report, WPPI Energy's Powering Ahead page and State of WPPI 2025 report, and Xcel's 2024 Upper Midwest plan.

Read the state utility commission dockets harvested for the scope and answered the 22 that matched no GEM plant; none is new gas generation. The Custer engine docket 2345-CE-100 was withdrawn in January 2022 and the Custer turbine is 24.5 MW, below the threshold.

Read the state air permits for the data center campuses at Mount Pleasant, Port Washington, Beaver Dam and Madison, and the city, village and county meeting records harvested for Kenosha, Caledonia, Racine, Beaver Dam, Port Washington and Milwaukee.

Checked the 45 active Wisconsin power plant air facilities in the federal enforcement database and the 46 Wisconsin turbine and engine permits in the federal control technology clearinghouse against GEM; every one not in GEM is below 50 MW, never built or not a power plant.
Searched the state business registry for the project companies of Red Oak Ridge, Foundry Ridge, Forest Junction, Union Depot and Port Washington, and for names tied to the new queue requests.
Searched the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel and the Wisconsin Examiner for gas plant, power plant, combustion turbine and data center stories since 2024 and tied each project they name to GEM.
irp_summary: State draft Strategic Energy Assessment 2026: 5,400 MW of new or upgraded gas by 2032; every named row is in GEM or this batch, and the Gas TBD rows are on the watch list.

WEC Energy Group: South Oak Creek, Paris engines, Port Washington upgrade, Foundry Ridge, Red Oak Ridge, Elm Road and Weston gas switches and Fox North are in GEM; about 917 MW of unnamed turbines and engines is on the watch list.
Alliant: Neenah and Sheboygan Falls upgrades finished in June 2026, Edgewater 5 gas switch is in GEM, the Riverside 2004 block is added, and the Columbia gas switch is on the watch list.
Madison Gas and Electric: its shares of Elm Road, West Riverside and RockGen are in GEM, Fitchburg is added, and the Columbia gas switch is on the watch list.
Xcel Northern States Power Wisconsin: Wheaton is the only Wisconsin gas item; the firm gas resources in the 2024 Upper Midwest plan are in Minnesota.
Dairyland: Elk Mound is added; Nemadji Trail is cancelled in GEM; no other gas project is named.
WPPI Energy: about 400 MW of gas with no site is on the watch list.

qa.question: Should the 2004 Riverside combined cycle block become its own plant, apart from the West Riverside block that GEM now holds under this plant?
qa.finding: The federal generator file lists two plants at the Beloit site: plant 55641 Riverside Energy Center (CTG1, CTG2 and STG1, 674.9 MW from 2004, owned only by Wisconsin Power and Light) and plant 64020 West Riverside Energy Center (CTG3, CTG4 and STG2, 723.2 MW from 2020, shared by six owners). GEM's plant carries the West Riverside unit, its shared owners and the EIA code 55641 of the older plant.
qa.recommendation: Keep the 2004 block as unit CC1 at this plant for now with Wisconsin Power and Light as its owner, and ask the GOGPT team lead whether the two blocks should be split into Riverside and West Riverside plants with their own owners and EIA codes.
qa.researcher_notes: Open the federal file at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx and go to the Operating sheet. Filter Plant ID to 55641 for the 2004 block and to 64020 for West Riverside. The plant-level owner list in GEM gives the West Riverside shares, which do not fit the older block. Alliant's 2025 annual report lists the Riverside Energy Center as a Wisconsin Power and Light station.

Plant 64020 West Riverside Energy Center is listed apart, with CTG3, CTG4 and STG2.
Alliant Energy annual report for 2025. Its list of Wisconsin Power and Light generating stations names the Riverside Energy Center and gives 17.5 MW for the engines there.

newunits.researcher_notes: GEM's only gas unit at Riverside is CC_set, 723 MW from 2020, which is the newer West Riverside block (federal plant 64020, shared owners). The older block is missing. The federal monthly generator file for September 2026 (Operating sheet, plant 55641 Riverside Energy Center) lists CTG1 198.9 MW, CTG2 198.9 MW and STG1 277.1 MW, operating since June 2004 and owned by Wisconsin Power & Light Co, 674.9 MW in all. The state air permit for the site describes four gas-fired combined cycle turbines in all and a project to raise the 2004 block's output from 625 MW by replacing its turbine parts. The Public Service Commission draft Strategic Energy Assessment, Table B-8, counts that as 156 MW of Riverside upgrades in 2028, and MISO request J3156 (100 MW, Townline Road, Rock County) is its grid request. Seven 2,500 kilowatt Caterpillar black start engines (17.5 MW in Alliant's 2025 annual report) also sit at the site and are below the unit threshold.
